title: AI-generated textures would leave watermarks/clues that it was generated by AI. Is this also valid for AI-generated 3D models?
author: GhostGuyBroke

comments.author: VisibleBoard8186
comments.body:
I mean it should be common sense at this point but let me paste this quick info here anyway: 

Removing Clues and Watermarks with AI

* Researchers have developed specific no-box removal frameworks like this neural-network-based tool, which uses frequency decomposition to suppress amplified noise and erase invisible image signatures without ruining visual quality. \[[1](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.15364)\]
* **Denoising and Style Transfer:** Passing an AI-generated texture through a secondary image-to-image AI model, a neural filter, or a heavy upscaler can scramble or smooth out the embedded statistical distribution of the original generation.
* **Manual and Structural Edits:** Rotating, cropping, adding slight grain, or re-saving textures through various compression formats can disrupt the delicate, invisible frequency markers detectors look for. \[[1](https://medium.com/activated-thinker/why-ai-watermarks-are-easy-to-remove-042794e908f1)\]

comments.author: florodude
comments.body: Right now the clue is the 3d model itself, mostly. The UV unwrapping would be another clue, and the textures would be another clue.

replies.author: florodude
replies.body: Does their newest version REALLY have it good? I use tripo for props and it's better, but I wouldn't call it "manual quality" would you?

comments.author: Cubey42
comments.body: No, not really. I think trying to obfuscate AI use isn't a good idea tho. Yeah AI backlash is scary but being caught in a lie is worse.

replies.author: tomato-shadow
replies.body:
I would even go further and say that, in general, people tend to be a lot more critical of trying to pass off AI generated content as real art than they are critical of gen AI usage as a whole.

If you're honest and upfront about it, at worse, people just won't play your game and you might get some criticism. If you lie and try to deceive them, people that would have ignored it will go out of their way to call you out.

And regardless, we're at a point where so much content is AI generated that people are naturally trained to recognise it, no matter how good you think it looks. No matter how much you try to obfuscate, lie and deceive people, they'll know. Watermark or not. 

Just own it and focus on making good quality stuff. It honestly just makes me think of someone picking up drawing and saying their kid drew it to avoid criticism lol. Criticism is good, it's what pushes us to improve.

replies.author: KitchenPoltergeist
replies.body: This is so important it should be in some sort of sub FAQ
